cells.tense: You are with what someone feels while the way ahead stays unclear, and you don't rush to close it.
cells.ask: Stay with one person's feeling for five minutes without reaching for a solution. When you leave it, write one line about what settled by itself.
cells.core: You can sit with what someone feels while the road isn't clear yet, and your footing holds. The not-knowing doesn't make you reach in and fix it. You let the feeling be what it is and stay in the room while it moves. That is rarer than it looks, and you don't make a production of it.\n\nWhat feeds this is structure: a hand that holds rather than presses. This balance isn't a resting place. It keeps only while you keep choosing it, and the toll is quiet — staying present when you'd rather resolve something and be done. A little more built ground underneath, and this steady contact is free to feed whatever wants to grow next from here.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a resolution that hasn't arrived and won't be written by force.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been pushing toward a clear answer. Leave it unanswered for two days, and each day write one line about what is true right now.
cells.core: You're pushing for a clear shape before it's here. Somewhere ahead is the moment it all resolves, and you're working to force it — reading the room harder than anyone asked, hoping enough attention will produce an answer. The effort is spending the very thing that makes people want to be near you.\n\nWhat brings you back is letting something end. Not all at once — just the one person's uncertainty you've been carrying for them, the one decision you keep rehearsing. A steward who holds everything ends up holding nothing. Let the unclear thing stay unclear, and let what's finished go quietly, and the contact comes back warm instead of strained.

cells.tense: You stopped offering yourself to the room, and the door you walked out of is behind you now.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you actually think about something unclear between you. Plain version only. Don't manage how they take it.
cells.core: You used to be steady with people while things were unclear, and somewhere along the line it started costing more than it gave. The way ahead got too foggy and you stepped out of the room with what people feel — what's left is distance, and it reads like not caring. It isn't that. You didn't lose your footing. You just stopped spending it.\n\nWhat wakes it is saying something true out loud. Calibrate — check what you actually think against what the other person says, not against your worry about it. Honest words, said with care, put you back in contact with the room, and from there it can start again.

cells.tense: You are already steadying the room, and you are filing it under something else.
cells.ask: Name one moment today when you kept something steady for someone. Say quietly to yourself that you did that. Notice what it costs to claim it.
cells.core: In the conversations you smooth, the silences you let breathe, the feeling you don't rush past — the work is running, and it runs quietly. If anyone asks, you'll say you were just being sensible, or that nothing was going on. Keeping things steady for people is real. The credit isn't claimed.\n\nWhat brings it into the open isn't more feeling — it's a plainer thought about it. Notice the pattern without dressing it up. Not the story of why you're like this, just the shape: there is a moment where something stayed steady because you stood there. That kind of seeing is enough to turn an unmarked habit into something you can own.
